checks.observed: 'A piece of jewelry marked 18K gold is 18 parts gold mixed with six parts of another metal. A piece marked 14K gold is 14 parts gold mixed with 10 parts of another metal.' / 'If you're thinking about buying a piece of gold jewelry but don't see a trademark along with the karat mark, don't buy it.' / 'The phrase "solid gold" means the gold item isn't hollow.' / defines gold filled, gold overlay, rolled gold plate (RGP), gold electroplate, vermeil, gold flashed, gold washed.

eCFR states 'Displaying title 16, up to date as of 10/21/2026'. Section headings read: 23.3 Misrepresentation as to gold content; 23.4 Misuse of the word 'vermeil'; 23.7 Disclosure of surface-layer application of rhodium; 23.8 Misrepresentation as to products containing more than one precious metal; 23.9 Misrepresentation as to content of pewter; 23.10 Additional guidance for the use of quality marks. 23.3(b)(1) reserves unqualified 'Gold' for 24-karat; 23.3(c)(1) bars 'solid' wording for hollow articles; 23.4(b) requires sterling silver + >=10K gold at 2.5 microns for 'vermeil'; 23.10 contains the trademark/quality-mark paragraph citing 15 U.S.C. 297.

'the actual fineness of such gold or alloy shall not be less by more than three one-thousandth parts than the fineness indicated by the mark' and '...shall not be less by more than three one-thousandth parts, in the case of a watchcase or flatware, or than seven one-thousandth parts, in the case of any other such article'.

Heading: 'Stamping plated articles.' (b) requires a trademark or name of the person applying any quality mark, in lettering at least as large as the quality mark and as close as possible to it. This section was cited on standards.html but had no sources.json entry before this pass.
